lesson.subtitle: Lesson 30 -- The Question You Did Not Expect
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rodrigo Luiz | Lesson 30 -- The Question You Did Not Expect
lesson.grammar_point: clarification and repair chunks (Sorry, do you mean...? / Could you say that again? / Let me check and come back to you)

listenings.text: Hi Rodrigo, it's Claire. I have three questions after your KPI presentation. First: you said the cost decreased. Sorry, do you mean the cost per kilo or the total cost? Second: is the delivery number for October, or for the quarter? Third: can you send me the data for the new line? No problem if you need to check. Just come back to me on Friday. Thanks!

Good question, Pierre. Sorry, do you mean the energy cost or the transport cost? Ah, the energy cost. OK. Honestly, I don't have the exact number here. Let me check, and I will come back to you tomorrow morning. Is that OK?

extra_audio.text: At the forum, Pierre asked Rodrigo a difficult question about the cost. Rodrigo did not understand the question. He said: sorry, do you mean the cost per kilo? Pierre said: yes, exactly. Rodrigo said: let me check the data and come back to you. The next day, he sent the number by email.

paras: After the KPI forum, the directors post their questions online. Some questions are easy. Some questions are difficult.
Pierre, Purchasing Director, Paris: "Rodrigo, you said the cost decreased by three percent. Is that the cost per kilo or the total cost? And why did it decrease?"
Ana, Operations Manager, Mexico: "Your delivery is very good. Can you explain your process? We want to use it in Mexico."

Rodrigo answers: "Thank you, Ana. Sure, I can explain it in our next call. Pierre, good question. It is the cost per kilo. I don't have the exact data here. Let me check and come back to you on Monday."
